title: Meshfree kernel approximation and conservative sph

items.title: Meshfree cell quadrature and fill radius
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open. Write $B(x,r)$ for the open Euclidean ball from [[def-metric-ball]] with distance induced by [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. A family of cells is **locally finite** here when every compact subset of $\Omega$ meets only finitely many cells. A bounded set is **Jordan measurable** when its Jordan inner and outer contents agree ([[def-jordan-inner-and-outer-content]]). A **cell particle rule** is a nonempty locally finite family of bounded Jordan-measurable cells $C_j\subseteq\Omega$ whose interiors are disjoint and whose union covers $\Omega$ up to their shared boundaries, together with nodes $x_j\in C_j$ and positive volumes $V_j=\int 1_{C_j}$. The cell volume integral is Riemann-defined and equals the Jordan content ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]). Its fill radius is $h=\sup_j\sup_{y\in C_j}|y-x_j|$, using the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]; require $0<h<\infty$. Assume finite constants $C_V,C_L>0$ satisfy $V_j\le C_Vh^d$ and the local volume bound

$$\sum_{j:C_j\cap B(x,r)\ne\varnothing}V_j\le C_L(r+h)^d$$

for every $x\in\mathbb R^d$ and $r>0$. For continuous $g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ with compact support contained in $\Omega$ (support as in [[def-support-and-compactly-supported-riemann-integral-in-rn]]), define $Q_hg=\sum_jV_jg(x_j)$; local finiteness makes this sum finite. At kernel width $\varepsilon$, an evaluation point is **interior** when $B(x,R\varepsilon+2h)\subset\Omega$. For periodic calculations, use the periodic extensions of the field and particle rule on $\mathbb R^d$, so no kernel support is truncated.

The cell rule is integration-compatible: for every continuous $g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ with compact support contained in $\Omega$, only finitely many cells meet $\operatorname{supp}(g)$, every cell integral appearing below is Riemann-defined, and
$$\int_\Omega g(y)\,dy=\sum_{j:C_j\cap\operatorname{supp}(g)\ne\varnothing}\int_{C_j}g(y)\,dy.$$
This finite partition identity is part of the quadrature data.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in this definition.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Scaled symmetric compactly supported kernel family
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$. An **admissible smoothing kernel** is a radial function $W\in C_c^2(\mathbb R^d,[0,\infty))$, supported in the closed Euclidean ball $\overline B(0,R)$ of some radius $R>0$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), with $\int_{\mathbb R^d}W(z)\,dz=1$. Here radial means $W(z)=w(|z|)$ for some function $w:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, and $C_c^2$ means twice continuously differentiable with compact support. All vector norms are the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and $\|D^2W\|_\infty$ uses the induced operator norm. Throughout this pair, $L^\infty$ norms are suprema of Euclidean norms, and norms of multilinear derivatives are the induced operator norms. Compactly supported integrals use [[def-support-and-compactly-supported-riemann-integral-in-rn]], where $\operatorname{supp}f$ is the closure of the set on which $f$ is nonzero.

For $\varepsilon>0$ define the scaled kernel $W_\varepsilon(z)=\varepsilon^{-d}W(z/\varepsilon)$. Write $M_0=\|W\|_\infty$, $M_1=\|\nabla W\|_\infty$, $M_2=\|D^2W\|_\infty$, $m_2=\int |z|^2W(z)\,dz$, and $m_3=\int |z|^3|\nabla W(z)|\,dz$. The norm functions and moment integrands are continuous with compact support. They are bounded and Riemann integrable on a bounding Jordan box by [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]], so these constants are finite.

For continuous $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$, define the full-space smoother and its kernel-gradient operator by
$$S_\varepsilon f(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x-z)W_\varepsilon(z)\,dz,\qquad D_\varepsilon f(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(y)\nabla W_\varepsilon(x-y)\,dy.$$
For each fixed $x$, both scalar integrands and every component of the vector integrand are continuous and compactly supported, hence Riemann integrable on a bounding Jordan box by [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]. Thus the displayed integrals exist as compactly supported Riemann integrals; the vector integral defining $D_\varepsilon f$ is taken componentwise.

This page fixes $\varepsilon$ in the finite-particle system. Limits $\varepsilon\to0$ are used only in the stated kernel-bias and joint-refinement results.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in this definition.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Fixed-width regularized conservative SPH particle system
items.statement:
Fix d,N≥1, positive masses m_1,…,m_N, ε>0, the kernel W_ε from [[def-scaled-symmetric-compact-kernel-family]], and a pressure map P∈C¹((0,∞)×R,R). Positions q_i and velocities v_i lie in R^d with the Euclidean inner product from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and specific internal energies e_i lie in R. Define

$$\rho_i(q)=\sum_{j=1}^Nm_jW_\varepsilon(q_i-q_j),\qquad p_i=P(\rho_i,e_i),\qquad A_i=\frac{p_i}{\rho_i^2}.$$

The state domain is U={ (q,v,e): ρ_i(q)>0 for every i }. On U, the fixed-width semidiscrete system is

$$\dot q_i=v_i,\qquad \dot v_i=-\sum_{j=1}^Nm_j(A_i+A_j)\nabla W_\varepsilon(q_i-q_j),\qquad \dot e_i=A_i\sum_{j=1}^Nm_j(v_i-v_j)\cdot\nabla W_\varepsilon(q_i-q_j).$$

A controlled tube is a compact subset of U on which ρ_i≥ρ_*>0 for every i. The system is semidiscrete: time remains continuous while the spatial state is represented by finitely many particles. It has fixed masses and fixed ε, includes the displayed matched internal-energy equation, and contains no artificial viscosity. No continuum Euler convergence is part of this definition.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in this definition.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Cellwise oscillation bound for particle quadrature
items.statement:
Let g be compactly supported and Lipschitz with constant L_g, meaning |g(y)−g(x)|≤L_g|y−x|, with supp(g)⊂Ω, and use the cells and nodes of [[def-meshfree-cell-quadrature-and-fill-radius]]. Define osc_C(g)=sup_{y,z∈C}|g(y)−g(z)| and let J_g={j:C_j∩supp(g)≠∅}. Then

$$\left|\int_\Omega g(y)dy-Q_hg\right|\le\sum_{j\in J_g}V_j\operatorname{osc}_{C_j}(g)\le 2hL_g\sum_{j\in J_g}V_j.$$

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Symmetry cancels the first kernel moment
items.statement: For the kernel W and its scaled family W_ε of [[def-scaled-symmetric-compact-kernel-family]], the first moment vanishes: ∫zW(z) dz=0 and ∫zW_ε(z) dz=0 for every ε>0.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Derivative moments of a compact radial kernel
items.statement:
For W from [[def-scaled-symmetric-compact-kernel-family]] and coordinate indices j,k,l,

$$\int \partial_kW(z)\,dz=0,\qquad \int z_j\partial_kW(z)\,dz=-\delta_{jk},\qquad \int z_jz_l\partial_kW(z)\,dz=0.$$

Also m₃=∫|z|³|∇W(z)|dz is finite.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Scaling identities for kernel moments and derivatives
items.statement: For the scaled kernels of [[def-scaled-symmetric-compact-kernel-family]] and every ε>0, supp W_ε⊂\overline B(0,Rε), ∫W_ε=1, ∫zW_ε(z)dz=0, and ∫|z|²W_ε(z)dz=ε²m₂. Pointwise, ∇W_ε(z)=ε^(−d−1)∇W(z/ε) and D²W_ε(z)=ε^(−d−2)D²W(z/ε); consequently their sup norms equal ε^(−d−1)M₁ and ε^(−d−2)M₂.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: SPH pressure forces are equal-opposite and central
items.statement: For the system in [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]], set g_ij=∇W_ε(q_i−q_j) and define the force contribution F_ij=−m_im_j(A_i+A_j)g_ij. Radial evenness gives g_ji=−g_ij and g_ii=0, so for i≠j, F_ji=−F_ij; also F_ij is parallel to q_i−q_j (the zero vector is allowed).

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Second-order convolution bias for an interior C² field
items.statement:
Let f∈C²(R^d) have bounded Hessian and define S_εf(x)=∫f(x−z)W_ε(z)dz. Then for every ε>0 and x∈R^d,

$$|S_\varepsilon f(x)-f(x)|\le \frac{m_2}{2}\varepsilon^2\|D^2f\|_\infty.$$

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Explicit local Lipschitz bound for the regularized SPH vector field
items.statement:
Let K be a nonempty compact convex subset of the positive-density domain of [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]]. Use ||z||#=max_i{|q_i|,|v_i|,|e_i|}, M=Σ_im_i, V=sup_{z∈K}max_i|v_i|, K₁=||∇W_ε||∞, K₂=||D²W_ε||∞, and a(ρ,e)=P(ρ,e)/ρ². Define A₀=max_{z∈K,1≤i≤N}|a(ρ_i(q),e_i)|, A_ρ=max_{z∈K,1≤i≤N}|∂_ρa(ρ_i(q),e_i)|, A_e=max_{z∈K,1≤i≤N}|∂_ea(ρ_i(q),e_i)|, and A_Lip=2MK₁A_ρ+A_e. By [[thm-extreme-value-metric]], these maxima are finite and attained, since K is nonempty compact and the functions involved are continuous. Then the full state vector field F is Lipschitz on K with constant

$$L=\max\{1,\ M(2K_1A_{\mathrm{Lip}}+4A_0K_2),\ 2MVA_{\mathrm{Lip}}K_1+2MA_0K_1+4MA_0VK_2\}.$$

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Linear and angular momentum are conserved by semidiscrete SPH
items.statement: Every C¹ solution of [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]] conserves total linear momentum P=Σ_im_iv_i and the antisymmetric angular-momentum tensor J=Σ_im_i(q_i⊗v_i−v_i⊗q_i), where (a⊗b)_kl=a_kb_l.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: The matched internal-energy equation conserves total semidiscrete energy
items.statement: Every C¹ solution of [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]] conserves H=Σ_im_i(|v_i|²/2+e_i). The identity uses exactly the displayed matched internal-energy equation.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Second-order bias for the kernel particle gradient
items.statement:
Let f∈C³(R^d) have bounded third derivative and define D_εf(x)=∫f(y)∇W_ε(x−y)dy. Then for every ε>0 and x∈R^d,

$$|D_\varepsilon f(x)-\nabla f(x)|\le \frac{m_3}{6}\varepsilon^2\|D^3f\|_\infty,$$

where ||D³f||∞ is the supremum of the operator norm of the trilinear derivative.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Explicit cellwise error for kernel value and gradient quadrature
items.statement:
Assume the cell rule of [[def-meshfree-cell-quadrature-and-fill-radius]], h≤ε≤1, x is interior, and f∈C¹(R^d) is bounded with bounded first derivative. Define

$$Q^0_{\varepsilon,h}f(x)=\sum_jV_jf(x_j)W_\varepsilon(x-x_j),\qquad Q^1_{\varepsilon,h}f(x)=\sum_jV_jf(x_j)\nabla W_\varepsilon(x-x_j).$$

Let S_εf(x)=∫f(y)W_ε(x−y)dy and D_εf(x)=∫f(y)∇W_ε(x−y)dy. There is C=C(d,R,C_L,W), independent of ε,h,x, such that

$$|Q^0_{\varepsilon,h}f(x)-S_\varepsilon f(x)|\le Ch\bigl(\|\nabla f\|_\infty+\varepsilon^{-1}\|f\|_\infty\bigr),$$

$$|Q^1_{\varepsilon,h}f(x)-D_\varepsilon f(x)|\le Ch\bigl(\varepsilon^{-1}\|\nabla f\|_\infty+\varepsilon^{-2}\|f\|_\infty\bigr).$$

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Joint fill-distance and kernel-width refinement for value and derivative consistency
items.statement:
Assume the hypotheses of [[thm-meshfree-particle-kernel-quadrature-error]] and let f∈C³(R^d) have bounded derivatives. There are constants C₀,C₁, independent of ε,h and the interior point x, such that

$$|Q^0_{\varepsilon,h}f(x)-f(x)|\le C_0\varepsilon^2\|D^2f\|_\infty+C_1h\bigl(\|\nabla f\|_\infty+\varepsilon^{-1}\|f\|_\infty\bigr),$$

$$|Q^1_{\varepsilon,h}f(x)-\nabla f(x)|\le C_0\varepsilon^2\|D^3f\|_\infty+C_1h\bigl(\varepsilon^{-1}\|\nabla f\|_\infty+\varepsilon^{-2}\|f\|_\infty\bigr).$$

Thus ε→0 and h/ε²→0 suffice for both value and derivative errors to vanish uniformly at interior points. Constants depend only on the fixed kernel, dimension, and cell regularity.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Local well-posedness of the regularized finite-particle SPH system
items.statement: For the system of [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]], U={z:ρ_i(q)>0 for every i} is open and its finite-dimensional vector field F is continuous and locally Lipschitz on U. From each initial state z₀∈U there is a unique local C¹ solution.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Forward Euler has first-order global error and preserves a margin tube for the regularized SPH ODE
items.statement:
Use the state norm ||z||#=max_i{|q_i|,|v_i|,|e_i|} on the finite-dimensional state space, and dist#(z,Kᶜ)=inf_{y∉K}||z−y||#. Let T>0 and let z(t), 0≤t≤T, be the unique solution from [[thm-regularized-sph-local-wellposedness]]. Let K⊂U be a nonempty compact convex set, with dist#(z(t),Kᶜ)≥δ>0 for every t. Assume B,L≥0, ||F(w)||#≤B for every w∈K, and Lip#(F|K)≤L. For an integer n≥1 set h=T/n, Z₀=z(0), and Z_{k+1}=Z_k+hF(Z_k). Put E_h=(Bh/2)(exp(LT)−1), which is zero when L=0. If E_h<δ, then every Euler state Z_k lies in K and

$$\max_{0\le k\le n}\|Z_k-z(kh)\|_\#\le E_h.$$

The tube margin and exact-path hypothesis are explicit. This result makes no energy- or momentum-conservation claim for the Euler time discretization.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

title: Meshfree kernel approximation and conservative sph — Examples

items.title: A normalized kernel loses constant reproduction when truncated at a boundary
items.statement: The claim that every normalized symmetric kernel preserves constants after truncation to a domain, even at a boundary point, is false.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Interior constant and affine reproduction by a symmetric kernel
items.statement: Let f(y)=a+b·y be affine on R^d. Full-space smoothing by an admissible symmetric kernel reproduces f exactly: S_εf(x)=f(x) for every ε>0 and x∈R^d.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Two SPH particles receive equal and opposite pressure forces
items.statement: For N=2 in [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]], write F_12 for the contribution of particle 2 to m_1v̇_1 and F_21 for the contribution of particle 1 to m_2v̇_2. These pair contributions are equal and opposite and act along the particle separation line.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: A disordered fixed-neighbor stencil can fail derivative consistency
items.statement: Keeping the same finite neighbor pattern in units of ε while refining ε alone guarantees consistency of a meshfree particle derivative. The following explicit periodic family refutes this claim for an affine field.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: A conservative positive-pressure SPH system can close a particle gap
items.statement: In a conservative SPH system with positive pressure, every adjacent particle gap has nonnegative initial relative acceleration. This is false: a third-particle pressure force can close a neighboring gap even while the semidiscrete invariants remain exact.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)
